To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the 1983 Amendments to the Social Security Act significantly increased SSDI participation among men and women aged 45 to 64, with an additional one percent of men and one and a half percent of women between these ages receiving benefits in 2006.

The 1983 Social Security Amendments increased the relative generosity of the SSDI program by reducing the relative generosity of retired worker benefits and that this change in program generosity significantly increased the enrollment of men and women in SSDI.

the 1983 Amendments to the Social Security Act increased Social Security Disability Insurance enrollment by about 0.7 percentage points among men and women aged 45 to 64, and that these increases are likely to continue in the coming decades.
